stories.headline: YIELDS SPIKE TO 4.55%, STOCKS RETREAT FROM RECORDS
stories.body: The S&P 500 fell 0.9% to 7,339 and Nasdaq slid 1.1% to 25,852 as the 10-year Treasury yield surged 9 bps to 4.55% — its highest in a year — on war-related inflation fears and a lack of breakthrough at the Trump-Xi summit. The Dow shed 495 points to 49,568, erasing Thursday's historic reclaim of 50,000.

stories.headline: WARSH TAKES FED CHAIR AS POWELL ERA ENDS; RATE HIKE ODDS HIT 45%
stories.body: Kevin Warsh officially becomes Federal Reserve Chair today as Jerome Powell's term expires. Markets have priced in a 45% probability of at least one rate hike in 2026 — up from just 1% a month ago — as persistently elevated oil prices from the Iran conflict keep inflation concerns front and center.

stories.headline: WTI TOPS $104 AS HORMUZ STRAIT RISK PERSISTS
stories.body: WTI crude surged above $104 per barrel on Friday, tracking toward a 10% weekly gain, as stalled U.S.-Iran peace talks kept supply disruption fears alive in the Strait of Hormuz. Rising energy costs are the primary driver of the current inflation spike and the shift in Fed rate-hike expectations.

stories.headline: CISCO SURGES 13.4% ON AI NETWORKING BOOM
stories.body: Cisco Systems jumped 13.4% after reporting strong earnings driven by explosive demand from hyperscalers building out AI-powered network infrastructure. The result highlights how enterprise networking is capturing a growing share of AI capex, even as broader tech sold off on rate fears Friday.

stories.headline: MICHIGAN RELOADS AS CHAMPION; KATZ DROPS FIRST 2026-27 BRACKET
stories.body: Reigning national champion Michigan has rebuilt impressively since winning the April 6 title. Andy Katz released his first bracket for the newly expanded 76-team 2026-27 tournament. With the NBA draft withdrawal deadline on May 27, final college roster decisions are imminent across the country.

stories.headline: PISTONS-CAVALIERS AND SPURS-WOLVES BOTH IN GAME 6 TONIGHT
stories.body: The Cavaliers (leading 3-2) host Detroit at 7 PM ET in a potential closeout Game 6, while the Spurs (leading 3-2) visit Minnesota at 9:30 PM ET. Cleveland took the series lead with a 112-103 road win in Game 5 on May 11; both teams face elimination pressure tonight.

stories.headline: 2026 NFL SCHEDULE DROPS; SEAHAWKS OPEN VS. PATRIOTS IN SUPER BOWL REMATCH
stories.body: The full 2026 NFL schedule released Friday. Seattle opens its title defense against New England on September 9 — a rematch of Super Bowl LX, which the Seahawks won 29-13. The season features a record nine international games and opens on a Wednesday for only the second time in league history.

stories.headline: TRANSFER PORTAL CLOSES; LSU AND PENN STATE LEAD MONSTER CLASSES
stories.body: The 2026 football transfer portal cycle has effectively wound down. LSU under Lane Kiffin assembled a class approaching 40 players; Penn State added nearly two dozen with coach Matt Campbell, who brought QB Rocco Becht from Iowa State as the cycle's most notable signal-caller transfer.

deepDive.title: Long-Duration Equities and the Discount Rate: Why Rising Yields Hit Tech Hardest
content: Tech stocks bore the brunt of Friday's selloff — the Nasdaq fell 1.1% even as some cyclicals held up — and the culprit was the 10-year Treasury yield surging to 4.55%, its highest level in a year. This is not coincidence. The link between long-end yields and growth stock valuations is one of the most direct and mechanical relationships in markets, and it was on full display today. Understanding the channel explains not just Friday's move, but why AI-driven rallies tend to be fragile when inflation is in the picture.

Every equity valuation is a discounted cash flow problem: the stock price equals the sum of all future earnings discounted back to the present. For a mature company like a utility or bank, most earnings arrive within five to ten years — so the discount rate matters, but not catastrophically. For a high-growth tech company, however, the bulk of expected earnings may be a decade or more into the future. A small change in the discount rate compounds over many years and destroys an enormous amount of present value. A stock pricing in 30% annual earnings growth for 15 years is extraordinarily sensitive to the rate used to discount year 12 earnings — and that rate is anchored to the 10-year Treasury yield.

This sensitivity is formalized by the concept of 'equity duration' — borrowing directly from fixed-income math. High-growth equities behave like long-duration bonds: small yield moves produce large price swings. The 2022 rate cycle made this viscerally clear. As the Fed hiked from 0.25% to 4.5%, the Nasdaq fell 33% while the Dow fell only 9%, because the Dow's component earnings are shorter-duration and less rate-sensitive. More precisely, a 100 basis point rise in the long-end yield typically reduces high-growth tech valuations by 20–30%, holding earnings expectations constant — a number that explains much of the tech wreckage seen during any serious rate-hike cycle.

Today's setup is particularly dangerous for tech because the rate pressure comes from the supply side — an oil shock from the Iran conflict driving CPI — rather than excess demand. The Fed is being forced into a potential hike with 45% market-implied probability, even as growth remains uncertain. New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, historically more hawkish than Powell, adds further uncertainty. If WTI stays above $100 and CPI stays elevated, Warsh signals the Fed will act, the discount rate pressure on tech won't relent — and yesterday's record highs could look premature in retrospect.
